articles.description: Oil prices rose on Friday as escalating tensions in the Middle East heightened concerns about further supply disruptions, offsetting US President Donald Trump’s latest efforts to increase domestic fuel production. Brent crude futures for December delivery rose 0.4% to $113.64 a barrel, while West Texas Intermediate futures for December gained 0.56% to $100.02. Both benchmarks were close to their highest levels since early May. The gains came after oil prices initially fell following Trump’s invocation of a Cold War-era law to encourage US oil and gas production and refining. However, prices reversed course as concerns over potential disruptions to Middle Eastern supply continued to dominate sentiment.
